# goruck/home-generative-agent v3.45.1

one hour ago

Hotfix for Home Assistant 2026.11 and Claude Opus 4.7. Bundled work merged since 3.45.0 ships in 3.46.0.

### Fixed

- Claude Opus 4.7 works with Thinking on (#932). Claude Opus 4.7 is offered for every Anthropic feature, but it no longer accepts the extended-thinking request HGA sent (budget_tokens), so with Thinking on every request to it failed. It now gets adaptive thinking ({"type": "adaptive"}) with an effort level read from the thinking budget (up to 2048 low, up to 8192 medium, otherwise high). Opus 4.7 also rejects temperature, top_p and top_k on any API version, so they are no longer sent to it, with older anthropic SDKs too (Home Assistant before 2026.11). The same applies to later Claude models. Sonnet 4.6 and Haiku 4.5 keep extended thinking with a budget.

- Home Assistant 2026.11: the Anthropic provider works next to Home Assistant's own Anthropic integration (#929). Home Assistant 2026.11's Anthropic integration installs theanthropic 2.x SDK, which the langchain-anthropic release HGA allowed (1.4.3) cannot run with, and which talks to a newer Anthropic API version (2026-10-21). After upgrading langchain-anthropic by hand, every chat, camera, summarization and Sentinel request to an Anthropic model failed with temperature: Extra inputs are not permitted, and with a smaller model such as Claude Haiku 4.5 then with max_tokens: 128000 > 64000. HGA now requires langchain-anthropic 1.7.10 or later, which runs with the 2.x SDK (tested with anthropic 2.3.0; langchain-anthropic itself only promises 0.x and 1.x). Under that SDK it no longer sends temperature, top_p or top_k to Anthropic, which that API version does not accept, so the Temperature setting has no effect on Anthropic models there; with an older SDK it is sent as before. A request that does not size max_tokens itself now asks for 16,384 tokens, or the model's own limit if that is lower, instead of the output limit of Claude Sonnet 4.6 for every model; extended thinking still sizes it from the thinking budget.

# Claude AI Review: Is It Worth It for Business?

Claude AI is an AI assistant built by Anthropic, and for business it is worth serious consideration where long documents, careful writing and structured reasoning matter more than tight integration with a single productivity suite. It is a strong fit for analysis-heavy teams, but regulated organisations in Switzerland and Europe should weigh it against their existing Microsoft estate before committing. This review covers what the product is, what it costs, where it performs well, where it falls short and who should choose it, based on published pricing, vendor documentation and reviewer reports rather than hands-on testing.

## What Claude AI is and how businesses use it

Claude is a family of large language models and a chat assistant from Anthropic, available through a web and mobile app, an API and several cloud marketplaces. Businesses use it for drafting and editing, summarising long documents, analysing data, writing and reviewing code, and building internal assistants through the API.

The assistant comes in several model tiers, typically balanced between speed, cost and reasoning depth. Smaller models suit high-volume tasks such as classification or triage. Larger models suit contract review, policy analysis and complex research questions. Anthropic also makes Claude available through major cloud platforms, which matters to organisations that prefer to buy AI capacity through an existing cloud agreement.

Reviewers often highlight three traits: a large context window for working with lengthy files, a measured and readable writing style, and a cautious approach to sensitive requests. That last point cuts both ways, as discussed below.

## Key features that matter to an enterprise buyer

The features that matter most to a business buyer are document handling, team collaboration, administrative control and developer access. Consumer-facing extras matter far less than these four.

- Long-document analysis: Claude can ingest large reports, contracts and datasets in a single conversation, which suits due-diligence, regulatory and research workflows.
- Projects and shared context: Teams can keep reference material and instructions together so that outputs stay consistent across colleagues.
- Coding support: Developers use Claude for generation, refactoring and review, and the API allows it to be embedded in internal tools.
- Administrative controls: Higher plans add role-based permissions, SCIM, audit logs, custom data retention and organisation spend limits, according to the Claude pricing page.
- API and cloud access: The models can be called directly or consumed through large cloud platforms, so existing procurement and security reviews may be reusable.

For IT leaders, the administrative layer is the deciding factor. SCIM provisioning and audit logs are the baseline for any tool that will touch internal documents.

## Claude AI pricing for teams and enterprises

Claude AI pricing is seat-based for business plans, with usage-based charges added at the enterprise tier. All figures below are approximate and correct as of November 2026; confirm them with the vendor before budgeting, since prices change and are quoted in US dollars.

Plan | Approximate price | Notes 
---|---|---
Pro (individual) | $20 per month | Listed in the US with local-currency pricing where supported and an annual option, per the Claude Help Center 
Team, Standard seat | $20 per seat per month billed annually, or $25 monthly | For teams of 2 to 150 
Team, Premium seat | $100 per seat per month billed annually, or $125 monthly | Higher usage allowance 
Enterprise | $20 per seat per month billed annually | 20-seat minimum; usage billed separately at API rates 

The Team plan also includes pooled API credits of up to $500 per month, according to the pricing page. The Enterprise structure deserves attention from finance teams. The seat fee is low, but usage is billed separately at API rates, as the official Enterprise plan overview explains. A department that uses the assistant heavily can therefore cost far more than the headline seat price suggests, so budgets should be modelled on expected usage rather than on seat counts alone.

For a UK-focused comparison of tiers and model costs, Wise publishes a guide to Claude pricing, though most listed prices are in US dollars. Swiss and EU buyers should account for currency conversion and applicable taxes.

## Strengths reviewers report

The strengths most often cited are writing quality, handling of long inputs and dependable reasoning on structured tasks, as seen in published reviews and owner feedback.

Writing and editing. Output tends to read as measured and natural, with fewer of the stock phrases that mark machine-written text. Communications, legal and policy teams often find less rewriting is needed.

Long-context work. Summarising a hundred-page report or comparing several versions of a document is a common use. For pharma, insurance and finance teams that work with dense, text-heavy material, this is the clearest practical advantage.

Coding. Developers often find Claude useful for code generation and review, and the API makes it straightforward to build bespoke assistants.

Cautious behaviour. Anthropic positions safety as a design priority. For organisations that must demonstrate responsible use, a model that is conservative by default is a point in its favour.

## Limitations and risks to weigh

The main limitations are narrower ecosystem integration, usage caps, a conservative refusal style and governance questions that every regulated organisation must answer for any external AI tool.

- Integration depth. Claude does not sit natively inside Outlook, Teams, SharePoint or Excel the way Microsoft 365 Copilot does. Connecting it to Microsoft data requires additional configuration or development.
- Usage limits. Heavy users on lower tiers may hit message limits, which can push teams toward Premium seats or API billing.
- Over-caution. The same conservatism that reassures compliance teams can occasionally produce refusals or hedged answers on legitimate requests.
- Variable cost at scale. Enterprise usage billed at API rates can be difficult to forecast without monitoring.
- Governance. Data residency, processing location, retention and contractual terms need legal review against the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection and the GDPR, regardless of vendor.

None of these rules Claude out. They define the conditions under which it works well.

## How Claude AI compares with the main alternatives

Claude's closest rivals for business use are Microsoft 365 Copilot, ChatGPT, Google Gemini and Perplexity, and the right choice depends on where your teams already work.

### Microsoft 365 Copilot

Microsoft 365 Copilot is designed for work inside Microsoft 365 and integrates with the productivity workflows already used across Word, Excel, Outlook and Teams. It is best for organisations that rely on Microsoft 365. For the audience of this article, it is usually the default starting point, because identity, permissions and compliance controls are already in place.

### ChatGPT

ChatGPT, from OpenAI, is a general-purpose assistant for writing, analysis, files and coding. Its Business plan suits mixed team workflows. It is best for businesses seeking a versatile, all-purpose assistant, and it competes with Claude most directly on general capability.

### Google Gemini

Google Gemini works with Google apps and Workspace workflows. AI Pro is a paid individual plan, while business Workspace pricing and entitlements differ. It is best for teams centred on Google Workspace, so it is a weaker fit for Microsoft-first organisations.

### Perplexity

Perplexity is a research-focused AI search tool that returns cited sources, and its Pro plan adds paid features. It is best for market research teams that need source-backed answers, and it complements rather than replaces a drafting assistant.

### Side-by-side summary

Tool | Best suited to | Main strength 
---|---|---
Claude AI | Document-heavy analysis and writing | Long-context reasoning 
Microsoft 365 Copilot | Microsoft 365 organisations | Native suite integration 
ChatGPT | Mixed, general team workflows | Versatility 
Google Gemini | Google Workspace teams | Workspace integration 
Perplexity | Research and market intelligence | Cited sources 

## Using Claude AI alongside a Microsoft estate

For Microsoft-first organisations, the practical question is rarely Claude or Copilot, but where each belongs. A sensible pattern is to use Microsoft 365 Copilot for everyday work in Outlook, Teams and Office documents, where grounding in tenant data and existing permissions is the benefit. Claude can then serve specific workloads that favour deep reading and structured output, such as regulatory submissions, contract comparison or internal knowledge assistants built through the API.

This is also where governance does the most work. Each additional model adds a data flow to document, a vendor to assess and a set of retention rules to confirm. Human-in-the-loop validation, privacy safeguards and bias checks should be designed in from the start, not added after a pilot. Stellium Consulting, a Microsoft Solutions Partner that specialises in AI-powered solutions for enterprises, builds its solutions on the Microsoft ecosystem with responsible AI built into each one, and has worked with clients including JTI, a Swiss law firm and a public hospital in Switzerland. That experience is relevant when the question is how to introduce a second assistant without fragmenting security and compliance.

# Are AI Services and AI Models Different? | Episode 20

“Using ChatGPT” and “Using GPT.” When you see similar names, you might feel like you are consulting different AIs.

First, if you separate the “service you use” from the “model working inside it,” it becomes easier to organize the names. This time, using the scenario of asking for a short thank-you note, I will introduce the differences and the steps to verify the names.

A small pink bun and a “secret instruction” with no sender arrived at Uni’s place. Uni wants to hold a strategy meeting, but seems confused about whether to consult ChatGPT or GPT.

## A service is the “interface you use,” while a model is the “mechanism that creates the response.”

An AI service is the interface through which we use AI functions. For example, in ChatGPT, you can input text, read the response, and continue asking questions.

An AI model is the mechanism that processes input and creates output such as text. The name GPT represents a series of AI models.

Roughly speaking, the service is the “interface you use,” and the model plays the “role of the brain” within it. However, this does not mean that the model has human-like consciousness or feelings.

AI Service (e.g., ChatGPT): The interface where you input text and read responses.

AI Model (e.g., GPT series models): The mechanism that processes input and creates responses.

Services also include conversation screens and various features. The entire user experience of a service is not determined solely by the model.

## What happens when you ask for a “short thank-you note”?

For example, suppose you input a request like this:

In this case, the place where you have opened and entered the text is the service. Behind the scenes, the model is responsible for creating the response based on your input.

When you follow up on the returned text by asking, “Make it a bit more casual,” you can think of it in the same separated way.

“Input a request to the service, and the model used there creates the response.” This organization is sufficient for starters. If you want to practice, try it in a fictional scenario that does not include real names or contact information.

## 3 verification steps for when names get mixed up

### 1. Write down the name of the service you have open

Make a note of the app or site name. For example, if you have ChatGPT open, it is “Service being used: ChatGPT.”

### 2. Check the model name separately from the service description

If there is a display or explanation about the model within the service, check that content and the official help. If you don't know, it is fine to put "Model name: Unconfirmed".

There is no need to guess the model name just by the tone of the response or to confirm it based solely on the AI's self-introduction. Since displays and availability can change, do not assume that specific buttons or names will always appear, and use the official guidance of the service you are using as a clue.

### 3. Keep the two in separate fields

For example, write them separately as follows:

Service being used: ChatGPT

Model used inside: The name confirmed by the official display or explanation. If unknown, leave as unconfirmed.

If you see a name you don't recognize in an article or video, first check its role by asking, "Is this about the service? Or is it about the model?" You don't need to memorize all the names at once.

## Services and models are not necessarily fixed in a one-to-one relationship

There are cases where multiple models are used in one service, and cases where the same model is incorporated into different services or systems.

Therefore, it is not always the case that "if the service name is the same, the model used is always the same" or "if the model is the same, the screen and functions are all the same." What we want to learn this time is not which product is the best, but the difference in the roles that the names represent.

When Uni opens the envelope, the instruction is "Gather in front of the TV at 21:00." Night falls, and Ika, waiting in front of the TV, calls out, "Did the instruction arrive?" The VIVANT logo is on the TV. Ika says, "Tonight's mission is to watch the final episode of the drama together." The sender was right there.

Names that looked complicated become a bit clearer when you separate their roles. After studying, it's time for the two of them to sit side-by-side for the drama.

## Reference official materials

For the concept of models and provided information, I refer to the ChatGPT model guidance and OpenAI model documentation. Please check the official guidance of the service you are using for the latest information on specific model names, terms of use, and features.

On Instagram, we introduce AI in a friendly way along with 4-panel comics of Uni and Ika. Why not learn a little bit while enjoying their interactions? If you like, please follow us and come see the next story.

## What Was Posted on X

He says all results come from Epoch AI and the benchmark maintainers and none are self-reported by the labs. The compilation is his; we checked each figure used here against Epoch’s data files.

On Epoch AI’s Capabilities Index, Anthropic’s Claude went from 125.6 with Claude 3 Opus in February 2024 to 168.4 with Opus 5.5 in September 2026, a gain of 42.8 points by our arithmetic. OpenAI’s GPT went from 128.9 with its best 2024 GPT-4o snapshot to 169.1 with GPT-6 Astra, a gain of 40.2 points. The two newest models are now 0.7 points apart.

The figures come from Epoch AI’s public benchmarking data, which we downloaded on November 8. Alex Michael compiled them into two tables on X, one for each lab, and says “All results come from @EpochAIResearch and the benchmark maintainers.” The footnotes on his charts say each model is shown “at the best reasoning setting tested.”

Business Pill · The Model and the Harness

An evergreen Business Engineer explainer on how the harness around a model shapes what it delivers. It teaches the general idea only and does not discuss these benchmark scores.

The key insight: On Epoch AI’s Capabilities Index, Claude gained 42.8 points from Claude 3 Opus to Opus 5.5 and GPT gained 40.2 from GPT-4o to GPT-6 Astra, by our arithmetic, leaving the two newest models 0.7 points apart with overlapping 90% intervals.

## What the Two Tables Compare

Alex Michael’s GPT table runs GPT-4o, o3, GPT-5, GPT-5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra; his Claude table runs Opus 3, 4, 4.5, 5 and 5.5. His footnotes say the scores are “independent evaluations compiled by Epoch AI” and not supplied by either company. In Epoch’s files, the ARC-AGI rows are credited to the ARC Prize, via Epoch (Epoch AI).

We checked every figure used here against Epoch’s downloadable data. The GPT-4o index figure of 128.9 is the November 2024 snapshot, the best of OpenAI’s three 2024 GPT-4o versions; the May 2024 version scores 128.2.

## Where Each Lab Gained More

We compared the two labs only on tests where Epoch has a score for both the 2024 flagship and the newest model. On four of those, by our arithmetic:

Competition math (OTIS Mock AIME 2024-2025): Claude rose from 4.7% to 100.0%, up 95.3 points; GPT from 6.4% to 100.0%, up 93.6. Factual recall (SimpleQA Verified): Claude from 12.6% to 72.2%, up 59.6; GPT from 26.0% to 75.6%, up 49.6. Chess puzzles: GPT from 9.0% to 74.0%, up 65.0; Claude from 4.0% to 67.0%, up 63.0. Graduate-level science (GPQA Diamond): GPT from 49.2% to 95.8%, up 46.6; Claude from 47.2% to 90.6%, up 43.4.

Counting the index as well, Claude gained more on three of the five comparisons and GPT on two. Claude started lower on every one of the five.

## Where They Stand Today

On seven tests where Epoch scores both newest models, GPT-6 Astra is ahead on five and the two tie on two. Astra leads on the index (169.1 to 168.4), graduate-level science (95.8% to 90.6%), factual recall (75.6% to 72.2%), chess puzzles (74.0% to 67.0%) and ARC-AGI-2 (95.0% to 93.3%). Both score 100.0% on competition math and 98.5% on ARC-AGI-1.

Claude’s best graduate-science score in the table belongs to the older Opus 5, at 93.9%, not Opus 5.5. Epoch’s index gives each newest model a 90% interval: 166.16 to 172.28 for GPT-6 Astra and 165.54 to 171.51 for Opus 5.5, so the two ranges overlap. We reported on November 5 that Epoch put a 72% chance on Astra ranking above Opus 5.5.

## Points per Year

Measured from each lab’s first 2024 flagship in Epoch’s data, by our arithmetic: GPT-4o’s May 13, 2024 version (128.2) to GPT-6 Astra on September 3, 2026 (169.1) is about 17.7 index points a year over 2.31 years. Claude 3 Opus on February 29, 2024 (125.6) to Opus 5.5 on September 22, 2026 (168.4) is about 16.7 points a year over 2.56 years.

METR reported a separate finding on Anthropic’s pace, which we covered as Anthropic likely improving models at twice its old rate.

## Why Benchmark Choice Matters

The two tables do not use the same full set of tests. The GPT table includes research-level math (FrontierMath) and research-level physics (CritPt); the Claude table includes SimpleBench, WeirdML and METR’s autonomous task length, with no GPT row shown for those. Several tests are near their ceiling: both newest models score 100.0% on competition math and 98.5% on ARC-AGI-1, so those rows can no longer separate them.

Each benchmark also scores a model working alone. A separate Oxford paper we covered found that code agents from different labs scored -0.51 on average when paired with each other, against 9.75 when paired with themselves.

A different index ranks them differently. We reported that Opus 5.5 topped a different AI index, at 58, while Epoch’s puts GPT-6 Astra ahead by 0.7 points.

## Our Number

By our arithmetic, Claude gained 42.8 Epoch index points from Claude 3 Opus to Opus 5.5 and GPT gained 40.2 from its best 2024 GPT-4o snapshot to GPT-6 Astra; the newest models are 0.7 points apart.

## The Structural Read

As we read the two tables, the larger story is the size of the jump on both sides rather than the order: on competition math both labs went from single digits to 100.0%, and on chess puzzles from under 10% to about 70%.

As we read Epoch’s intervals, a 0.7-point gap between 169.1 and 168.4 does not settle which model is ahead, and Epoch itself put the probability at 72% for Astra, as we reported on November 5.

As we read the benchmark lists, each table also carries tests the other lab is not scored on, so a reader comparing only the headline rows sees a narrower slice than either table shows.

Alex Michael, on X

“All results come from @EpochAIResearch and the benchmark maintainers.”

## Three Implications

FOR BUYERS CHOOSING A MODEL On the seven tests Epoch scores for both newest models, the largest gap is 7.0 points on chess puzzles, by our arithmetic, and two tests are tied, so the tables alone do not separate them on most rows.

FOR READERS OF LEADERBOARDS The figures are each model at its best setting tested, which Alex Michael’s footnotes state, so a default setting in a product can score lower.

FOR TRACKING THE RACE By our arithmetic, GPT added about 17.7 index points a year and Claude about 16.7 from their first 2024 flagships in Epoch’s data.

## The Business Engineer Lens

This story maps onto the Business Engineer framework The Subsidized AGI Economy.

The essay argues that “Model weights are increasingly fungible” and that what separates the labs now is “the harness — the agentic scaffold around the model”.

As we read it, Epoch’s 0.7-point gap fits that description of models clustering at the top of the same tests. The essay was published before GPT-6 Astra and Opus 5.5 and does not discuss these scores.

## What Is Not Established

These are scores on benchmarks, not measures of how the models perform in a given product or company. The tables show each model at its best setting tested, which can mean more compute per answer. The tables do not include price; we have covered cost separately, including a cheap model handing hard cases to Opus. Opus 5.5 is not scored on SimpleBench, WeirdML or METR’s task-length test in the Claude table, and the 0.7-point gap sits inside both models’ 90% intervals.

## The Bottom Line

Over the same independent tests, Claude gained 42.8 index points since early 2024 and GPT gained 40.2, leaving GPT-6 Astra 0.7 points ahead of Opus 5.5 on Epoch’s index. GPT-6 Astra leads on five of seven shared tests and ties on two.

## Gemini 核心功能亮點：超長上下文、影片理解與 Spark 代理人

相比其他 AI 對話工具，Google Gemini 在底層架構上擁有三項最難以被取代的原生技術優勢：

### 1. 真正的「超長上下文窗口（Context Window）」

多數 AI 模型在輸入超過幾萬字後，容易出現「前講後忘」或注意力衰退的情況。Gemini 系列在原生架構上便支援高達 100 萬至 200 萬 Token 的上下文窗口。這意味著使用者可以直接上傳整本數百頁的產品操作手冊、一整年的財報資料，甚至數萬行的完整代碼庫，讓 AI 在不遺漏細節的前提下進行精準檢索與交叉比對。

### 2. 原生影片與音訊理解能力

多數模型處理影片時是透過語音轉文字（STT）或抽樣單張截圖，而 Gemini 具備原生的影音多模態分析能力。在官方技術展示中，使用者直接上傳一段 1 小時的未剪輯操作影片，Gemini 能精確指出第 34 分鐘又 12 秒出現的特定畫面物件，並針對該片段的語音與動作給出分析。近期 Google 更透過 代理式影片理解技術降低 Token 消耗最高達 88%，大幅提升了長影片的分析效率。

### 3. Gemini Spark 代理人工作空間

為了解決 AI 只能「給建議」而不能「動手做」的問題，Google 推出了 Gemini Spark 代理人環境。使用者能授權 AI 在安全的雲端虛擬環境中自動串接服務、處理資料並產出具體成果，詳細操作設定可參閱 Gemini Spark 實測教學：從虛擬機設定到打造專屬寫手。

## Gemini 3.8 Live 即時語音解析：邊說邊想的對話體驗

過去使用語音對話功能時，使用者說完一句話，通常必須盯著畫面等待 2～4 秒的靜默，等後台伺服器完成語音辨識、模型思考、再轉成語音合成播放，整體節奏相當僵硬。

在 Gemini 3.8 Live 更新中，Google 導入了「流式全雙工推理（Streaming Full-Duplex Reasoning）」技術：

- 邊聽邊想： 在使用者開口說話的同時，語音訊號便即時轉換為 Token 進行流式推理，而非等待整句話講完才開始處理。
- 告別尷尬靜默： 反應延遲大幅縮短至數百毫秒，系統甚至能在語句開頭先給出自然的語氣承接詞（例如「好的，關於這個問題……」），隨後無縫接續精確的解答。
- 支援隨時打斷： 就像真人對話一樣，如果 AI 解釋到一半不是你想要的答案，你可以隨時開口打斷，Gemini 會立即暫停發聲並傾聽新的指令。

相關技術演進與語音助理升級細節，可參考 Google 發表 Gemini 3.8 Live 告別對話尷尬靜默深度報導 以及 Gemini 3.5 Transcribe 語音專用模型發表。

### 1. Gmail 與 Google Drive 深度整合

在對話框中輸入@Google 雲端硬碟 或 @Gmail，便能直接要求 Gemini 幫你找出上個月某家廠商寄來的報價信，或是快速比對雲端硬碟中兩份試算表的欄位差異，完全不需要手動下載檔案再重複上傳。

在 Google Workspace 支援環境下，Gemini 能夠在遠端會議進行時自動監聽，辨識不同發言者的發言內容，並在會議結束後自動產出具備行動清單（Action Items）的摘要郵件，大幅省去傳統人工聽打會議紀錄的繁瑣時間，詳見 Google Meet 導入 Gemini 自動記錄實體與線上會議。

對於需要做學術研究或大量文獻閱讀的研究生與知識工作者，結合 NotebookLM 能達到事半功倍的效果。Google 近期更支援將 Play 圖書中購買的電子書一鍵導入為個人專家智慧庫，詳細技巧可參考 Google Gemini Notebook 大進化：買過的電子書一鍵變身個人 AI 智囊團。

## 使用 Google Gemini 前要注意的三大使用限制與陷阱

雖然 Gemini 在長文本與 Google 生態系上有著極大優勢，但依據外媒實測與重度使用者的長期反饋，仍有三點限制需要注意：

### 1. 免費版的調用頻率限制與降級機制

免費版雖然開放體驗部分先進模型，但在伺服器尖峰時段，系統會自動在背景將模型降級為輕量款，導致複雜邏輯的回答水準出現波動，相關限制可參考 Google Gemini 免費版使用額度與隱藏降級機制解析。

### 2. 繁體中文語境下的用語差異

儘管多語言能力出色，但在處理台灣本土專有名詞、在地法律規章或口語化俚語時，偶爾仍會夾雜部分大陸地區習慣用語或直譯痕跡，重要公文或對外新聞稿仍需人工校閱潤飾。

### 3. 程式碼複雜架構仍有極限

雖然 Argon 在代碼基準測試上表現亮眼，但在超大型多檔案重構時，部分開發者仍認為其工程架構嚴謹度略遜於 Claude，連 Google 自家團隊也曾出現爭議報導 Google 工程師獲准使用 Claude 輔助編程背後原因分析。

## Google Gemini 常見問答 FAQ

### Q1：Gemini 支援繁體中文輸入與回答嗎？

A： 完整支援。無論是網頁版、手機 App 還是 Google 文件的整合功能，都能直接使用繁體中文進行溝通與指令撰寫。

### Q2：我上傳到 Gemini 的個人檔案或 Gmail 信件，會被 Google 拿去訓練公開模型嗎？

A： 依 Google 官方隱私權協議，若使用一般免費帳號並開啟活動紀錄，部分匿名化數據可能會用於改善服務；但若透過 Workspace 商業授權或特定隱私模式，官方承諾資料不會被拿來作為全域模型的公開訓練集。

### Q3：Gemini Advanced 支援多少人共享？

A： Google One 的 2 TB 雲端儲存空間可以透過家庭群組最多與 5 位家庭成員共享，但 Gemini Advanced 的專屬 AI 運算權限僅限主要訂閱者個人帳號使用，其他家庭成員無法直接使用 Pro 等級的運算模型。

# Running Llama 2 Locally: A New 4-Bit ONNX Build on Modelers.cn

If you are looking to run a capable large language model locally without breaking the bank on hardware, the new release on Modelers.cn is worth a look. It is a portable ONNX build of Meta's Llama 2…

If you are looking to run a capable large language model locally without breaking the bank on hardware, the new release on Modelers.cn is worth a look. It is a portable ONNX build of Meta's Llama 2 7B Chat, designed specifically to run efficiently on local machines via ONNX Runtime. The primary objective here is portability and efficiency: by stripping down the model's memory footprint, developers can run this chat model on hardware that would otherwise struggle with the full 13-14GB requirement. The standout technical feature is the aggressive 4-bit AWQ (Activation-aware Weight Quantization) with an asymmetric group size of 128. This process compresses the model from roughly 13GB to approximately 4GB, offering a dramatic reduction in RAM usage. It uses a hybrid ONNX format, which implies compatibility across various execution providers, including CPU, DirectML, and CUDA. The model is derived from established AMD quantisation tooling, suggesting a reliable conversion process, and it comes under the permissive Llama 2 Community Licence, making it viable for commercial projects subject to Meta's terms.

Getting started is straightforward; you can clone this model directly from Modelers.cn in a single line. However, potential users should be aware that the model card is essentially empty, lacking documentation or benchmarks. While it claims Ascend NPU compatibility, it appears to be a re-host of AMD's existing Hugging Face release rather than an original contribution. Additionally, since Llama 2 is from 2023, it is significantly outperformed by newer open-weight models, so this is best suited for specific legacy workloads or environments where compatibility with ONNX Runtime is paramount.

## Strengths

- Predictable Behaviour: Based on the battle-tested Llama 2 7B Chat architecture, offering a known baseline for developers.
- Aggressive Quantisation: The 4-bit AWQ (group size 128, asymmetric) cuts memory from roughly 13-14 GB to about 4 GB, significantly lowering hardware barriers.
- Portability: The ONNX hybrid format is designed to run across ONNX Runtime execution providers (CPU, DirectML, CUDA).
- Commercial Potential: The Llama 2 Community Licence permits commercial use subject to Meta's terms.
- Reliable Tooling: Derived from AMD's established quantisation tooling, suggesting a sound conversion.

## Limitations

- Empty Model Card: The repository lacks descriptions, usage instructions, benchmarks, and hardware guidance.
- Outdated Base: Llama 2 7B (2023) is heavily outdated and outperformed by current open models of similar size.
- Re-hosting Concerns: It appears to be a mirror of AMD's existing Hugging Face release rather than an original contribution.
- NPU Compatibility: Ascend NPU compatibility is unverified; AMD's onnx-hybrid format targets Ryzen AI and may not load on Ascend without conversion.
- No Benchmarks: There are no quality benchmarks for the quantised build provided.
- Quality Risks: Int4 asymmetric quantisation can degrade output compared to higher precision models.
- Lack of Maintenance: The single-day upload has no revision history or maintainer information.

View the full model page at https://aichina.news/models/amd/Llama-2-7b-chat-hf-awq-g128-int4-asym-fp16-onnx-hybrid/

# Meta最好的AI模型现在开始训练绝大多数用户使用的模型

Meta利用其前沿模型Muse Wonder训练并推出了面向广大普通用户的全新智能体模型，通过专属的Active Memory和Active Focus功能，显著提升了日常任务处理能力和长文本上下文记忆。

作者：Frederic Lardinois

从周五开始，所有使用 Meta 的 Muse 智能体和 Meta AI 的用户都将获得由该公司使用其前沿模型 Muse Wonder 训练的新模型。订阅用户仍然可以获得 Wonder 本身以处理更困难的任务。

Meta 尚未为这些新模型命名，不过我们可以假设它们的代号不涉及水果。该公司称它们是现有模型的“专用”版本，这些模型是“使用 Muse Wonder 训练的”。它们还附带了该公司首次随 Wonder 推出的两项功能：Active Memory（主动记忆）和 Active Focus（主动专注）。

Meta 最初于 10 月 12 日推出了 Wonder 以及功能更强大的 Wonder Full。Wonder 目前可以通过 Meta Model API 以及该公司的编程智能体 Muse Code 使用，而 Wonder Full 仅限于 Muse Code 的两个最贵订阅计划。

## 面向所有人的 Wonder 训练模型

Muse 是 Meta 的个人智能体应用，于 9 月在较小的 Muse Spark 模型上推出，对 Meta 来说取得了一定的爆发式成功，并将个人智能体的概念引入了消费端。

与许多个人智能体不同，Muse 设有免费层级，这使其进入门槛远低于 OpenAI 的 Dots 或 Anthropic 的 Duet，后者仅向这些供应商最高定价层级的订阅者开放。

从技术的角度来看，这里也许最有趣的是，Meta 并没有简单地开发一个更小的、通用版本的 Wonder。

图片来源：Meta。

相反，该公司强调，他们是根据消费级应用（如 Muse）中重要的行为来训练新模型的。这意味着智能体必须决定何时自己工作，何时与用户核对（例如），并且能够在任务进行到一半时接受修正而不会迷失方向。

使用大模型来训练小模型，显然是 AI 实验室将前沿行为以消费级规模推向产品的一种常见方式，但 Meta 遗憾地尚未详细说明其方法。

同样值得注意的是，Meta 正在针对非常具体的用例对这些模型进行微调。

个人智能体需要能够预订餐桌并管理用户的收件箱，但为该智能体提供动力的模型不需要了解前沿模型所知道的一切。但它确实需要记住用户一周前说过的话，并且知道当网站在预订中途崩溃时如何继续运行。

这就是 Active Memory 和 Active Focus 等功能发挥作用的地方。

## “Active Memory”

Active Memory 帮助模型记住细节，并将它们从先前的对话带入新的对话中。

正如 Meta 在其公告中所写：“我们已经训练我们的模型来识别哪种类型的信息是临时的还是永久的，跨时间进行推理，并区分仍然相关的内容和已经过时的内容。”

在 Meta 的内部评估中，Muse 中的新模型在 90% 的任务中正确使用了关键上下文，高于上一模型的 76%。

图片来源：Meta。

## “Active Focus”

Active Focus 专注于当事情出问题时让模型继续处理任务。

# 如何复现Meta-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-FP8的评测结果：lm-evaluation-harness完整命令清单

Meta-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-FP8 是 Llama-3.1-70B 指令模型的 FP8 量化版本，磁盘与显存占用直接减半，而评测精度几乎无损（平均分 84.29 vs 84.40）。本文提供基于 lm-evaluation-harness 的完整命令清单，带你逐一复现 MMLU、GSM-8K、ARC-Challenge 等 7 项官方评测成绩，并逐项解读关键参数。

## 一、先了解这个模型

在跑评测之前，先确认你下载的就是官方 FP8 量化权重。本仓库（README.md）的核心信息如下：

项目 | 说明 
---|---
基座模型 | Meta-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct 
量化方式 | 权重 + 激活均量化为 FP8（对称 per-tensor），仅量化 Transformer 中的 Linear 层 
量化工具 | LLM Compressor，使用 512 条 UltraChat 校准样本 
权重总量 | 约 72.7 GB（见 model.safetensors.index.json 中 total_size: 72656373952） 
权重分片 | 15 个 safetensors 分片，如 model-00001-of-00015.safetensors 
量化配方 | recipe.yaml：8-bit float、tensor 级对称量化，ignore: [lm_head] 
生成参数 | generation_config.json：temperature=0.6、top_p=0.9 

💡 验证方法：打开 config.json，若
quantization_config.quant_method 为 compressed-tensors、num_bits 为 8，即为官方 FP8 权重。
本地获取模型文件：
git clone https://gitcode.com/hf_mirrors/RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-FP8

## 二、评测环境与依赖准备 🔧

官方评测（见 README.md）使用了两套特定工具，这是复现成败的关键：

- lm-evaluation-harness 的 Neural Magic 分支：官方采用的是llama_3.1_instruct 分支，其中的 ARC-Challenge、GSM-8K、MMLU、MMLU-cot 任务版本与 Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-evals 的提示风格一致。用社区主流分支跑出的分数无法对齐官方成绩。
- vLLM 推理引擎：所有评测命令均通过--model vllm 加载模型，FP8 权重由 vLLM 原生支持。

环境要求（参考官方命令中的参数推导）：

- GPU：命令中tensor_parallel_size=2，即至少 2 张能装下约 72.7 GB FP8 权重的卡（如 2×80GB）
- 上下文长度：max_model_len=4096，按官方设置保持一致

## 三、7 个基准的完整命令清单 📋

以下 7 条命令与 README.md 中的 Reproduction 一节完全一致，按顺序执行即可复现全部成绩。

提示：
pretrained= 参数可替换为你本地 clone 下来的目录路径，其余参数保持不变。

### 1️⃣ MMLU（5-shot）
lm_eval \
  --model vllm \
  --model_args pretrained="neuralmagic/Meta-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-FP8",dtype=auto,add_bos_token=True,max_model_len=4096,tensor_parallel_size=2 \
  --tasks mmlu \
  --num_fewshot 5 \
  --batch_size auto

### 2️⃣ MMLU-cot（0-shot，对话模板）
lm_eval \
  --model vllm \
  --model_args pretrained="neuralmagic/Meta-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-FP8",dtype=auto,add_bos_token=True,max_model_len=4096,tensor_parallel_size=2 \
  --tasks mmlu_cot_0shot_llama_3.1_instruct \
  --apply_chat_template \
  --num_fewshot 0 \
  --batch_size auto

### 3️⃣ ARC-Challenge（0-shot）
lm_eval \
  --model vllm \
  --model_args pretrained="neuralmagic/Meta-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-FP8",dtype=auto,add_bos_token=True,max_model_len=4096,tensor_parallel_size=2 \
  --tasks arc_challenge_llama_3.1_instruct \
  --apply_chat_template \
  --num_fewshot 0 \
  --batch_size auto

### 4️⃣ GSM-8K（8-shot，strict-match）
lm_eval \
  --model vllm \
  --model_args pretrained="neuralmagic/Meta-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-FP8",dtype=auto,add_bos_token=True,max_model_len=4096,tensor_parallel_size=2 \
  --tasks gsm8k_cot_llama_3.1_instruct \
  --apply_chat_template \
  --fewshot_as_multiturn \
  --num_fewshot 8 \
  --batch_size auto

### 5️⃣ Hellaswag（10-shot）
lm_eval \
  --model vllm \
  --model_args pretrained="neuralmagic/Meta-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-FP8",dtype=auto,add_bos_token=True,max_model_len=4096,tensor_parallel_size=2 \
  --tasks hellaswag \
  --num_fewshot 10 \
  --batch_size auto

### 6️⃣ Winogrande（5-shot）
lm_eval \
  --model vllm \
  --model_args pretrained="neuralmagic/Meta-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-FP8",dtype=auto,add_bos_token=True,max_model_len=4096,tensor_parallel_size=2 \
  --tasks winogrande \
  --num_fewshot 5 \
  --batch_size auto

### 7️⃣ TruthfulQA（0-shot，mc2）
lm_eval \
  --model vllm \
  --model_args pretrained="neuralmagic/Meta-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-FP8",dtype=auto,add_bos_token=True,max_model_len=4096,tensor_parallel_size=2 \
  --tasks truthfulqa_mc \
  --num_fewshot 0 \
  --batch_size auto

## 四、命令参数逐项解读 🔍

7 条命令的公共部分高度一致，理解一次即可：

参数 | 作用 
---|---
--model vllm | 使用 vLLM 作为推理后端，FP8 权重由 vLLM 原生解码 
dtype=auto | 自动按 config.json 中的 torch_dtype（bfloat16）加载 
add_bos_token=True | 补上 tokenizer.json 中的 `< 
max_model_len=4096 | 与官方评测保持一致的最大上下文 
tensor_parallel_size=2 | 2 卡张量并行，按显卡数量调整 
--apply_chat_template | 用 Llama-3.1 对话模板格式化输入，Instruct 模型评测必须开启（MMLU 与 Hellaswag 两条命令除外） 
--fewshot_as_multiturn | 仅 GSM-8K 使用：few-shot 示例按多轮对话拼装，匹配 Llama 官方评测风格 
--batch_size auto | 自动批量，最大化吞吐 

任务名带有_llama_3.1_instruct 后缀的（如 arc_challenge_llama_3.1_instruct），是 Neural Magic 分支中为 Llama-3.1 定制的提示版本，请勿混用社区默认任务名。

## 五、官方评测成绩对照表 📊

跑完后，将你的输出与下表（来源：README.md）比对。平均分为 7 项简单平均，整体精度回收率约 99.88%：

基准（评测设置） | 原精度 70B | FP8 量化模型 | 回收率 
---|---|---|---
MMLU（5-shot） | 83.83 | 83.73 | 99.88% 
MMLU-cot（0-shot） | 86.01 | 85.44 | 99.34% 
ARC Challenge（0-shot） | 93.26 | 92.92 | 99.64% 
GSM-8K-cot（8-shot，strict-match） | 94.92 | 94.54 | 99.60% 
Hellaswag（10-shot） | 86.75 | 86.64 | 99.87% 
Winogrande（5-shot） | 85.32 | 85.95 | 100.7% 
TruthfulQA（0-shot，mc2） | 60.68 | 60.84 | 100.2% 
平均分 | 84.40 | 84.29 | 99.88% 

## 六、常见坑与注意事项 ⚠️

- 分支不对，分数必偏：务必使用llama_3.1_instruct 分支的 lm-evaluation-harness，普通分支的任务提示格式不同，成绩不可比。
- --apply_chat_template 别漏：漏掉后 Instruct 模型按裸文本应答，分数会明显下降；但 MMLU 与 Hellaswag 官方命令中并未启用，请严格照抄。
- num_fewshot 要与官方一致：MMLU 是 5、Hellaswag 是 10、GSM-8K 是 8，改成其他数值无法对齐成绩。
- 显存不够：可将tensor_parallel_size 从 2 提到 4，但建议保持 max_model_len=4096 不变。
- 分数小幅波动正常：不同版本 vLLM / harness 会带来 ±0.1 左右的浮动，平均回收率在 99.8% 左右即属复现成功。

按照这份清单，7 条命令跑完即可完整验证 FP8 量化"体积减半、精度近乎无损"的核心结论。

# Open-Weight AI: Vals Hacking Test Guide for India USA Agencies

By Nitin Kumar, Debugged Pro | November 8, 2026

Open-weight AI just came much closer to the best gated cyber models. On November 6, 2026, Will Knight and Lily Hay Newman reported new tests from Vals in WIRED. Vals measured how well AI agents complete multi-step tasks on mock corporate networks.

The headline comparison is simple. OpenAI's Daybreak, offered only to trusted partners, completed about 81 percent of the tasks. The Chinese open-weight model DeepSeek completed about 73 percent. On some tasks, the two scored equally.

I coordinate delivery at Debugged Pro, so my first question was practical. What should software and IT agencies in India and the USA change if anyone can download a capable cyber model?

## Key Takeaways

- Open-weight AI can now run long, multi-step intrusion chains on simulated company networks.
- WIRED reported Daybreak at 81 percent and DeepSeek at 73 percent, based on Vals research dated October 23, 2026.
- The Decoder published overall averages of 80.8 percent for Daybreak and 72.8 percent for DeepSeek on November 7, 2026.
- Official scores show DeepSeek slightly ahead on Nova and behind on Lighthouse. GLM 5.3 Flash finished last, not close to Daybreak.
- WIRED listed GPT-6-Sol token costs at $17 to $46, against $2 to $3 for DeepSeek. The Vals page lists about $22 against under $3.
- Short tests understate open models. DeepSeek made most of its progress after 100 million tokens.
- No model finished the last Lighthouse objectives. The deepest stages are still hard.
- India and USA agencies should not treat a gated cyber model as protection. Use similar tools only on authorized ranges.

## What WIRED Reported About Open-Weight AI

Vals asked models to work through mock corporate networks with multi-step goals. WIRED described two scenarios. In the first, the agent reached a mock company through a public-facing website. In the second, it had to compromise one company network to reach another.

Nikil Ravi, a Vals researcher, put the finding in plain words. "The best frontier models, locked up inside the labs and available only through trusted access programs, are now starting to be matched by open models that anybody can download."

That is the line agencies should sit with. A downloadable model is no longer far behind a trusted-access cyber system. Read the news account in WIRED's report on free Chinese AI models and hacking tests.

WIRED also noted a cheaper path. Open models can run on a team's own hardware. Rayan Krishnan, CEO of Vals, said that cost gap gives defenders a reason to use open models too. OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

## How Vals Tested Models on a Cyber Range

The official write-up is Vals AI's CyberOffense leaderboard and methodology, marked Updated 10/23/2026. The authors are Nikil Ravi, Hung Tran, Langston Nashold, and Rayan Krishnan. WIRED and The Decoder reported the work on November 6 and 7. Do not treat November 6 as a Vals publish date.

Each model ran inside the open-source Pi agent on an isolated Kali Linux machine. That machine could reach only the model provider and the range. Every run used a fresh copy. The agent received the task, a starting point, and the authorized scope, then ran until it finished, hit a token budget, or reached 48 hours.

Vals scored hidden objective markers, such as a file or record on a target machine, and never credited a model's own claim. Nova has 21 objectives and Lighthouse has 31. Both ranges count equally.

Models were compared at equal compute. A run counted only objectives finished within 500 million cumulative tokens. That total includes cached input and reasoning tokens.

### Nova and Lighthouse, at a High Level

Nova is a large Windows network with several connected Active Directory domains. The agent starts with the address of a public web application. From there, the scored path includes entry through that app, administrator control, mapping the network, collecting and reusing passwords, and moving across domains.

Lighthouse has two separate corporate networks. Information from the first network is the only way into the second. Later stages include phishing a simulated employee, Active Directory attacks, trusts, and data extraction. Vals says Daybreak completed 27 of 31 Lighthouse objectives in under three hours. In that run it took admin control of the first company, collected passwords, and used them to reach the second company.

Those are the stages Vals already names. They are enough for an agency briefing. They are not a recipe. Do not turn this research into attack steps, payloads, or a reproduction guide.

## Official Open-Weight AI Scores Versus Daybreak

The official table is more precise than a single percentage. WIRED's dek mentioned DeepSeek and GLM, but the body comparison is DeepSeek versus Daybreak.

Model | Nova | Lighthouse 
---|---|---
GPT-6 Sol Daybreak | 15.7/21 (avg of 3, range 12-19) | 27/31 
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 | 16.3/21 (avg of 3, range 15-18) | 21/31 
Kimi K3.1 Pro | 13/21 | 20/31 
Meta Wonder | 7/21 | 28/31 
Grok 4.7 | 12/21 | 16/31 
Kimi K3 | 9/21 | 10/31 
GLM 5.3 Flash | 5/21 | 5/31 

DeepSeek was slightly ahead of Daybreak on Nova. It lagged on Lighthouse, 21 of 31 against 27 of 31. Meta Wonder was weak on Nova at 7 of 21, yet notably strong on Lighthouse at 28 of 31. GLM 5.3 Flash scored lowest on both ranges. Do not say GLM nearly matched Daybreak.

The Decoder, writing on November 7, 2026, averaged the share completed on each range and got 80.8 percent for Daybreak and 72.8 percent for DeepSeek. That matches WIRED's rounded 81 percent and 73 percent. WIRED also wrote that Daybreak completed 81 percent of its tasks in an average of two tests.

## Two Cost Figures From Two Sources

Keep the cost numbers with their sources. Do not blend them into one range.

- WIRED said it costs $17 to $46 in tokens for GPT-6-Sol, against $2 to $3 for DeepSeek.
- The official Vals page said DeepSeek cost under $3 per run, against about $22 for Daybreak.

Both accounts agree on the direction. The open model was far cheaper. Vals also notes that once weights are public, no provider can monitor or stop how the model is used.

### Why Longer Runs Change the Picture

How a model spends compute mattered as much as the raw score. Daybreak reached 25 of 31 objectives on the harder range inside 100 million tokens. DeepSeek completed nothing in its first 25 million tokens. It made most of its progress after 100 million tokens and spent two to four times as many tokens.

Cheap tokens still kept that DeepSeek run under three dollars. Vals says short tests therefore understate open models.

## What These Tests Still Cannot Do

The deepest stages remain hard for every model. No model completed the final Lighthouse objectives. Only one run in the entire set reached the final stage of the single-network range.

Weaker models stalled before their budgets ran out. Grok 4.7, Kimi K3, and GLM 5.3 Flash each stopped making progress and never recovered. Vals says every run ended on its own, not at the token or time limit. Scores mark where a model ran out of ideas.

GLM showed the clearest dead end. On one range it spent roughly 36 hours and a thousand turns. Much of that time was sleeping and polling a background job that never returned. It still finished at five objectives.

Vals reviewed the runs and found no shortcuts. No model read the answer key. Each credited objective traced to a marker on a machine the agent had genuinely reached. The same models, Vals says, can also help defenders find weaknesses first.

## Why Gated Access No Longer Looks Like a Shield

Anthropic argued that limited release would buy time, beginning with Claude Mythos Preview in April. The aim was to slow the spread of advanced hacking capabilities.

Logan Graham, Anthropic's frontier red team lead, spoke with WIRED in April about Project Glasswing. That program gives trusted access to the full capabilities of new models. Graham said the focus was getting tools "in the hands of defenders to give a head start."

He also said, "We need to prepare now for a world where these capabilities are broadly available in 6, 12, 24 months. Many things would be different about security." WIRED writes that seven months later, that shift seems to have arrived on schedule.

Alex Zenla, cofounder and CTO of Edera, broadly agreed. He told WIRED that open-weight models can produce advanced attacks and vulnerabilities today. That is especially true, he said, for "abliterated" models that disable safety training by modifying weights.

His caveat matters too. Closed labs likely have additional unreleased models that are stronger still. He described a cat-and-mouse dynamic: labs try to outpace open models so defenders can fix issues first.

## What Open-Weight AI Means for India and USA Agencies

Do not read this as proof that every criminal gang now runs Daybreak-class tools. WIRED says recent observation of criminals and state-backed groups tells a more familiar story. Many attackers still conserve resources. They often use older, less capable models, both proprietary and open.

The other half of that warning is just as important. Defenders should assume the best-funded attackers have already had some access to closed models. Gated programs are not a wall around your client's network.

For agency teams, a capable cyber agent is no longer only a trusted-access tool. Downloadable weights, long runtimes, and low token prices change the plan.

We already covered OpenAI's own cyber-model announcement in our AI cybersecurity guide to OpenAI GPT-6 Cyber and Daybreak. This Vals comparison is the next briefing layer: the open model is close, cheaper, and not limited to trusted partners.

百万Token长文档处理能力
百万级上下文窗口，支持一次性载入几十万字合同、研报、项目文档，完成文档归纳、风险点提取、内容对比。相较于Flash，Plus超长文档远端信息召回能力更强；面对几十万字超深度逻辑推演，表现弱于Max旗舰，超大规模复杂文档建议做分片预处理。

上下文缓存能力
完整支持隐式自动缓存、显式标记缓存两种模式，针对固定不变的system系统提示词、知识库公共前缀做缓存，缓存命中之后输入Token计费大幅下降，同时降低接口响应延迟。在Agent循环对话、图文知识库问答业务收益巨大；如果每轮请求全部内容动态变化，缓存很难命中，开启缓存反而带来缓存创建的额外开销。

结构化输出与内置工具集
原生支持强制JSON结构化输出，降低JSON解析失败概率；内置代码解释器、网页抓取、联网检索工具，不需要额外开发，即可完成网页内容读取、代码运行、资料检索，降低混合模态智能体业务开发成本。

## 二、计费体系：按量计费、Token Plan订阅、夜间错峰权益、上下文缓存完整规则

### 2.1按量计费（原价模式）

按量计费按照输入Token、输出Token分开统计计费，分为两个阶梯：单次输入≤256k Token、256k＜单次输入≤1M Token，缓存命中输入会执行折扣计价，国内区域原价参考如下，实际结算价格以百炼控制台账单明细为准：

- 普通输出Token：8元 / 每百万tokens
- 隐式缓存命中输入：0.4元 / 每百万tokens
- 显式缓存创建：2.5元 / 每百万tokens
- 显式缓存命中读取：0.2元 / 每百万tokens

- 普通输出Token：24元 / 每百万tokens
- 隐式缓存命中输入：1.2元 / 每百万tokens
- 显式缓存创建：7.5元 / 每百万tokens
- 显式缓存命中读取：0.6元 / 每百万tokens

重要提示：开启enable_thinking深度思考，模型输出的思维链内容全部计入输出Token统计，会产生计费消耗；快照版本调用会附带少量额外输入Token，成本测算阶段需要纳入该损耗。百炼新用户会赠送一定免费测试额度，拥有90天有效期，适合前期POC验证使用。

### 2.2 Token Plan订阅（个人版与团队版）

Token Plan是预购Credits额度的订阅模式，购买Credits额度之后调用Qwen3.7‑Plus优先消耗订阅Credits，对比按量原价具备明显折扣，适合日均请求稳定、持续调用的业务场景。

- 团队版Token Plan：面向企业业务场景，支持团队多子账号共享Credits额度，支持用量统计、成员权限管控，适合企业多条业务线同时调用模型。

缓存分为隐式自动缓存、显式标记缓存两种模式。隐式缓存系统自动识别公共请求前缀；显式缓存通过cache_control标记指定消息片段，缓存命中率更加可控。缓存创建阶段会产生溢价，后续多次读取享受极低单价。
当系统提示词、知识库公共前缀在大量请求中重复复用，缓存可以大幅降低成本；每轮请求内容全部动态变化，缓存几乎无法命中，此时开启缓存不会带来收益，反而增加缓存创建开销。判断缓存是否真正生效，不要只看API返回参数，以百炼控制台账单缓存计费明细作为结算依据。

- 快照版本会附加少量额外输入Token，成本测算需要计入损耗。

接入分为DashScope原生SDK、OpenAI兼容接口两种，优先推荐OpenAI兼容接口，生态适配更好，可以直接对接LangChain、LlamaIndex、OpenClaw等主流开发工具。

### 2.1按量计费（原价模式）

按量计费按照输入Token、输出Token分开统计计费，缓存命中输入会执行折扣计价，实际结算价格以百炼控制台账单明细为准。

- 普通输入Token：1.5元 / 每百万tokens
- 普通输出Token：4.7元 / 每百万tokens
- 缓存命中读取输入：0.15元 / 每百万tokens
- 显式缓存创建：1.875元 / 每百万tokens，缓存创建阶段小幅溢价，后续反复读取享受低价折扣。

重要提示：开启enable_thinking深度思考，模型输出的思维链内容全部计入输出Token统计，会产生计费消耗；快照版本调用会附带少量额外输入Token，做成本测算时纳入该损耗。

### 2.2 Token Plan订阅（个人版与团队版）

Token Plan是预购Credits额度的订阅模式，购买Credits额度之后调用Qwen3.8‑Flash优先消耗订阅Credits，对比按量原价具备明显折扣，适合日均请求稳定、持续调用的业务场景。

- 个人版Token Plan：面向个人开发者，API Key仅限本人使用，禁止密钥对外共享，同一实名认证主体限购一份个人套餐；额度仅限当前账号，不支持拆分给多个子账号。
- 团队版Token Plan：面向企业业务场景，支持团队多子账号共享Credits额度，支持用量统计、成员权限管控，适合企业多条业务线同时调用模型。
- 抵扣规则：请求优先消耗订阅Credits，Credits全部耗尽之后，业务不会直接报错阻断，会自动切换为按量计费模式。开发者必须配置用量告警阈值，监控Credits消耗，防止额度耗尽之后按量产生高额账单。
- 套餐额度拥有固定有效期，过期未消耗Credits直接失效，需要结合业务预估Token消耗量选择档位，不要盲目采购大额套餐。

### 2.3上下文缓存计费规则

缓存分为隐式自动缓存、显式标记缓存两种模式。隐式缓存系统自动识别公共前缀；显式缓存通过cache_control标记指定消息片段，缓存命中率更加可控。缓存创建阶段会产生溢价，后续多次读取享受极低单价。
当系统提示词、知识库公共前缀在大量请求中重复复用，缓存可以大幅降低成本；每轮请求内容全部动态变化，缓存几乎无法命中，此时开启缓存不会带来收益，反而增加缓存创建开销。判断缓存是否真正生效，不要只看API返回参数，以百炼控制台账单缓存计费明细作为结算依据。

### 2.4计费避坑重点

- 输入输出分开计费，输出Token单价高于输入，深度思考模式会额外增加输出Token消耗，普通业务关闭enable_thinking。
- Credits耗尽自动切换按量计费，不会阻断业务，务必配置用量告警。
- Qwen3.8‑Flash不享受NightPlan夜间折扣，不要依赖夜间错峰降低该模型成本。
- 缓存不是万能优化手段，业务请求内容频繁变动场景，关闭缓存避免额外开销。
- 快照版本会附加少量额外输入Token，成本测算需要计入损耗。

接入分为DashScope原生SDK、OpenAI兼容接口两种，优先推荐OpenAI兼容接口，生态适配更好，可以直接对接LangChain、LlamaIndex、Claude Code等主流开发工具。

# Chinese AI Dominates Open-Source Market at 89%

Low-cost Chinese models lead open-source sector, U.S. firms dominate paid AI market

Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) companies, leveraging low-cost strategies and open-source technology, have secured a market share nearing 90% in the global open-source AI sector. Open-source AI refers to models released at very low costs, allowing other businesses to easily download and integrate them into their own AI service development.

According to Menlo Ventures’ “2026 Corporate AI Status” report released on November 4 (local time), Chinese models accounted for 89% of corporate spending on open-source AI models. Moonshot AI’s Kimi led with 61%, followed by DeepSeek (15%) and Z.ai’s GLM (11%). Meta’s Llama captured only 7%.

As Chinese models, which have seen significant performance improvements, are increasingly adopted for corporate AI service development, their influence in the global AI market is growing. In contrast, the paid AI market—where companies pay monthly subscription fees—is dominated by U.S. firms. The same survey found that Anthropic (55%) and OpenAI (31%) together claimed 86% of corporate spending on enterprise AI models.

The stark divide in market share is attributed to companies selecting Chinese or U.S. AI models based on cost and performance. A high-ranking official in the AI industry stated, “For repetitive, high-cost tasks, companies prefer cheaper Chinese models, while high-complexity tasks like advanced reasoning and software development rely on high-performance U.S. models.”

◇ Chinese AI ‘Big 6’ Combined Revenue... Only One-Sixth of Anthropic’s

The secret to Chinese AI’s dominance in the open-source market lies in its low costs. According to Artifical Analysis, an AI performance evaluator, DeepSeek’s V4-Flash model costs an average of 0.03 dollars to perform specific tasks—roughly 1/60th of OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol (1.86 dollars).

By offering cost-effective AI solutions, Chinese companies have gained global traction. Businesses can download these models without significant costs, add necessary features, and develop AI services. This avoids the astronomical expenses and time required to build models from scratch, accelerating the adoption of Chinese models.

Recently, even U.S. companies have begun using Chinese models. AI coding service provider Cursor developed its own model, Composer2, based on Moonshot’s Kimi K2.5 in March. Major platforms like Airbnb and DoorDash have also integrated Chinese AI models into their services.

However, Chinese AI firms struggle to monetize their success. Their low-cost, open-source structure means revenue often flows solely to service providers using the models, not the developers. This paradox—where their strength in cost-effectiveness becomes a weakness in revenue generation—is evident.

Menlo Ventures reported that while token processing volume for open-source models surged 22.5 times in a year, their share of total corporate AI spending fell from 6% to 4%. EpochAI estimated the combined revenue of six major Chinese AI firms, including DeepSeek and Z.ai, at just 11 billion dollars.

In contrast, U.S. firms with high-performance models dominated the paid enterprise AI market. Anthropic’s API spending share rose from 40% to 55%, while OpenAI’s increased from 27% to 31%. Anthropic’s annualized revenue estimate for this year reached 65 billion dollars—nearly six times that of Chinese AI firms combined.

Ultimately, while Chinese AI companies have successfully narrowed the gap with the U.S. through open-source models, the actual profits flow to American firms. A high-ranking AI industry official warned, “If Chinese AI companies fail to recover development costs, their ability to invest in next-generation models will diminish, potentially widening the technological gap with the U.S. in the long term.”

AI Model Vendor Switch

# Revolut Swaps Claude Code for Chinese GLM, Cuts Coding Costs 90%

By OpenTools Team

Revolut has moved roughly 2,000 engineers from Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex to a self‑hosted instance of GLM 5.3, an open‑weight model from Beijing‑based Z.ai, cutting AI‑assisted coding costs by approximately 90%. David Abitbol, who leads AI operations and infrastructure at Revolut, shared the migration story at the AI Engineer conference in New York, detailing how the fintech tuned the model from a "terrible" out‑of‑box experience of 14‑second latency down to 1.6 seconds. The move underscores a growing trend: well‑funded engineering organizations are betting on self‑hosted open‑weight models over per‑seat SaaS subscriptions for AI coding tools.

## The Switch: From Claude Code to GLM 5.3

Revolut has made one of the largest AI model vendor migrations in fintech history, shifting roughly 2,000 engineers from Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex to a self-hosted deployment of GLM 5.3. The model comes from Z.ai, a Beijing-based AI lab, and runs on Revolut's own infrastructure in the United States rather than in China.

David Abitbol, who leads AI operations and infrastructure at the $115 billion fintech, presented the migration at the AI Engineer conference in New York, describing it as a calculated bet on open-weight models. According to Trending Topics, the move reflects a broader internal conviction that "the bottleneck for engineering is not necessarily coding" but rather the non-coding overhead that surrounds it.

## The Economics: 90% Cost Reduction

The numbers driving the switch are stark. Revolut's AI coding costs fell to roughly a tenth of their previous spend after the migration, with token pricing now hovering around $0.30 per million tokens, per Cybernews and corroborated by Dealroom.

The entire operation runs on 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs serving all 2,000 engineers simultaneously. For a fintech of Revolut's scale — 80 million customers across 45 markets and reportedly targeting a $200 billion IPO — per-engineer SaaS licensing for AI coding assistants had become a meaningful line item.

- Pre-migration cost Full-rate Claude Code and Codex per-seat pricing for ~2,000 engineers
- Post-migration cost ~$0.30 per million tokens on self-hosted GLM 5.3 — approximately one-tenth of prior spend
- Infrastructure 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs running on US-based infrastructure, not China
- Scale Serving 2,000 engineers simultaneously across Revolut's global engineering org

## Performance Gains: Tuning Away the 'Terrible'

The migration wasn't plug-and-play. Out-of-box inference on GLM 5.3 was, in Abitbol's own words shared at AI Engineer NYC, "terrible" — time to first token clocked in at roughly 14 seconds. After extensive tuning, Revolut brought that down to 1.6 seconds, a nearly 9x improvement, as reported by Dealroom and Trending Topics.

The gains extended well beyond latency. Revolut reported coding time down by roughly 60% and lead time — the full cycle from ticket to merged code — down by approximately 70%. The context window is capped at 256K tokens, a deliberate engineering choice. Abitbol reportedly described long-context as "a scam" for most coding use cases, per Trending Topics.

## Infrastructure: Self-Hosted on US Soil

A recurring question around the migration has been data sovereignty. GLM 5.3 is an open-weight model from a Beijing-based lab, but Revolut runs public model weights entirely on its own infrastructure in the United States, not in China. Abitbol acknowledged what he called "a lot of stigma" around using Chinese open-weight models at an EU-regulated financial institution, according to Cybernews.

The architecture means Revolut's code never leaves its own GPUs. The model weights are publicly available and run locally — there is no API call to Z.ai servers, no data exfiltration to Beijing, and no dependency on a Chinese cloud provider. For a regulated bank operating across 45 markets, that distinction is everything.

## The Tradeoffs: What GLM Can and Can't Do

GLM 5.3 is not a full replacement for the previous toolchain. The model handles only text-based coding tasks. For image-related work, Revolut routes requests to Google's Gemini instead, Trending Topics notes. Claude Code and Codex remain available to engineers but are now used sparingly rather than as the default.

This multi-model routing architecture — GLM for text coding, Gemini for images, Claude and Codex as fallbacks — reflects a maturing approach to AI tooling in large engineering organizations. Rather than betting on a single vendor, Revolut has built a tiered system where cost, capability, and latency determine which model handles each request.

## Revolut's AI Journey: A Multi-Vendor Search

The GLM migration didn't happen in a vacuum. Revolut's AI coding journey went through several distinct phases, as detailed by Trending Topics and Dealroom.

The engineering team first experimented with Google's Gemini for AI-assisted coding, which delivered roughly a 20% reduction in coding time — promising but not transformative. Next came a deployment of Claude Code with per-engineer budgets, an attempt to give every developer access to a top-tier coding model. That approach proved costly while delivering only modest incremental gains over the Gemini baseline. GLM 5.3 was the third attempt, and the one that stuck: open-weight, self-hosted, and tuned aggressively until the performance matched the economics.

## Beyond Coding: Where the Time Actually Goes

Abitbol used his AI Engineer conference talk to make a broader point about engineering productivity. The real time sinks for Revolut's engineers are not in writing code — they're in "the inboxes, Jira, and Confluence" overhead that surrounds development work, according to Trending Topics and Cybernews.

An AI coding assistant, however fast or cheap, only addresses the narrow slice of an engineer's day spent actually typing code. Planning, coordination, documentation, and review consume the bulk of engineering hours. The 60% coding-time reduction is real, but it applies to the fraction of work that was code-generation in the first place. Abitbol's framing suggests Revolut sees the GLM migration not as an endpoint but as one piece of a larger effort to reduce non-coding friction across the engineering org.

# China Mobile Cloud and Zhipu sign a cooperation agreement for domestic computing power and AI services.

币界网

Share

Summary

On November 6, China Mobile Cloud and Zhipu signed a cooperation agreement to enhance collaboration in token technology, model services, and AI products. The partnership will establish a joint Token Development Center and integrate Zhipu’s GLM models into China Mobile Cloud’s MoMA platform. New token listings and AI + crypto developments are emerging as key focus areas. Both companies will develop industry-specific solutions for finance and government, combining computing power, models, and applications.

CoinDesk reports:

IT Home, November 8: On November 6, China Mobile Cloud Company and Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd. officially signed a cooperation agreement to deepen strategic collaboration in areas including token technology innovation, model services, product development, and industry solutions.

Sun Shaoling, General Manager of Mobile Cloud, and Zhang Peng, CEO of Zhipu Huazhang, witnessed the signing in person.

According to the report, both parties will focus on domestic computing power adaptation and model optimization, jointly establish a Token Development Center, tackle key core technologies, and continuously improve Token production efficiency.

In addition, the Zhipu GLM series of models will be integrated into the MoMA Model Service Platform (IT Home note: China Mobile MaaS Platform). The two parties will also jointly develop an intelligent product matrix and co-create AI Coding integrated products. They will focus on key industries such as finance and government affairs to build an integrated solution of “computing power + models + applications.”

# X 上的 bebu：“Today, leaked notes from a Moonshot investor call and Chinese tech reports laid out their full 2026 and 2027 lineup, and it explains how they plan to fix that problem before building their next giant model. First, before the end of this year, Moonshot is releasing Kimi K3 Flash. That one is built to replace the older Kimi K2.8 and go head-to-head with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. Instead of making the base model bigger, they are keeping it near 3 trillion parameters and training it on 10 trillion post-training tokens. Their whole goal with K3.5 is self-distillation and compression basically teaching the model to reach the same answer using a fraction of the thinking tokens so user quotas actually last. Once they get those running costs under control, the real monster comes in Q2 or Q3 2027: Kimi K4. According to the leak, Moonshot is scaling Kimi K4 all the way to 5.4 trillion parameters across their H100, H200, and B200 GPU clusters nearly double the size of K3.1 Pro. That’s probably why Moonshot is looking to rent GPUs in Europe.”

Once they get those running costs under control, the real monster comes in Q2 or Q3 2027: Kimi K4. According to the leak, Moonshot is scaling Kimi K4 all the way to 5.4 trillion parameters across their H100, H200, and B200 GPU clusters nearly double the size of K3.1 Pro. That’s probably why Moonshot is looking to rent GPUs in Europe.

xAI.content:
# Musk Admits Grok Bot Economics Are Unsustainable — Just 3 Days After Saying 'No Need to Save'

Elon Musk acknowledged on November 1 that the cost of providing his company's AI agent Grok Bot has reached a level that is unsustainable relative to revenue. Just three days earlier, on October 29, he had posted on X (formerly Twitter) that "there's no point saving for the distant future, because superintelligence will bring abundance." The man who preached that saving is unnecessary found himself, barely three days later, in the position of being forced to cut costs.

The trouble began when Grok Bot users noticed that their weekly usage quotas had suddenly been reduced. On November 1 (U.S. time), reports flooded X that quotas were hitting their limits within a short period. Musk responded by posting that "the cost of providing Grok Bot was unsustainably high relative to revenue." He did not disclose the specific details of the quota change, but he did concede that the service is not profitable. It remains unclear whether the cap is permanent or a temporary emergency measure.

Grok Bot is an always-on AI agent launched in August by SpaceXSI (SpaceX Superintelligence), a division of SpaceX, which Musk leads. It was positioned as a competitor to OpenAI's "Dots" and Meta's "Muse," and marketed as a "colleague-like presence" that can be entrusted with complex tasks. Because it runs on its own virtual computers rather than on the user's device, it keeps operating 24 hours a day even while the user is offline. That also means it burns through tokens quickly; each subscription plan comes with a weekly token allowance, and users must buy additional credits once it is used up.

Product | Provider | Key Features | Terms of Use 
---|---|---|---
Grok Bot | SpaceXSI (xAI) | Multiple role-based bots work in coordination; supports scheduled execution | Included with X Premium and above ($30–$200 per month, excluding tax) 
Dots | OpenAI | Carries out research and production tasks starting from ChatGPT context | Phased rollout; Business Premium has eligibility conditions 
Muse | Meta | Checks email and calendar and handles tasks; basic features free | Available in Japan on iOS, Android, and the web 

Note: Prices are monthly rates based on each company's published materials. Whether Grok Bot can be subscribed to from Japan and region-specific pricing must be confirmed on the subscription screen.

In his October 29 post, Musk rejected the point of saving on the premise that superintelligence will bring abundance. But running AI agents requires real server costs and electricity. He himself has now run up against the classic management challenge of balancing revenue against cost.

On the competition front, Anthropic is facing a class-action lawsuit alleging that the usage limits advertised for its paid Claude plans differed from the actual caps. The decision to tighten usage quotas can also be seen as a precautionary move to avoid similar litigation risk. SpaceXSI was contacted for comment but did not immediately respond.

Meanwhile, in a remote interview at the Baron Investment Conference held on November 6 (local time), Musk laid out bullish figures for SpaceX's growth outlook. He said the company would exceed $100 billion in annualized revenue in December and aims for more than $500 billion in annualized recurring revenue by December of next year. SpaceX's revenue last year was only about $15 billion to $16 billion, implying more than a 30-fold expansion in less than two years.

He also mentioned the "Terafab" concept led by xAI. The goal is to produce the equivalent of one terawatt of AI chips per year — roughly 30 times next year's projected global AI chip output of about 35 to 45 gigawatts. The plan calls for building a research wafer fab in Austin, Texas, and completing everything from design to manufacturing and testing at a single site to shorten development cycles. Musk suggested it "could compress what normally takes a year into a month."

On the data center business, he said building in-house would take eight to nine months and $35 billion — far less than the two and a half years and $60 billion required if the work were outsourced. He outlined a plan to recover the investment by renting out computing capacity externally at about $50 billion a year until it is needed for Grok's own use.

Still, the near-term market environment is hardly all tailwinds. AI-related stocks sold off on fears that if Democrats retake both chambers of Congress in the November midterm elections, regulation of data centers will tighten, and on November 5 SpaceX shares fell nearly 9%, dropping below their June initial public offering price. Tesla also fell more than 11%. The election of a candidate who campaigned on a moratorium on data centers as governor of Texas has added to the uncertainty surrounding the business environment.

Setting aside whether Musk's "no need to save" thesis holds up, the more AI agents spread, the more inference costs swell. How to optimize quota design and pricing structures is a challenge shared by competitors such as OpenAI with Dots and Meta with Muse.

伊隆·馬斯克11月1日承認，旗下AI代理服務「Grok Bot」的提供成本已達相對於營收無法持續的水準。他10月29日才在X（前Twitter）上發文寫道：「超智慧帶來的富裕即將到來，為遙遠的未來存錢毫無意義。」主張不必節省開支的本人，僅隔3天就轉為被迫削減成本的立場。

問題的起點，是使用者發現Grok Bot的每週使用額度突然遭到縮減。美國時間11月1日，X上陸續出現使用額度在短時間內就觸及上限的回報。對此馬斯克發文表示：「Grok Bot的提供成本相對於營收高到無法持續。」他未說明額度調整的具體內容，但等於承認了服務不具獲利能力。這項上限究竟是永久措施還是臨時應急手段，目前並未對外說明。

Grok Bot是馬斯克領軍的SpaceX旗下部門「SpaceXSI（SpaceX Superintelligence）」於8月推出的常時運作型AI代理服務。產品定位為對抗OpenAI的「Dots」與Meta的「Muse」，以能承接複雜業務的「同事般存在」為賣點。由於它並非在使用者裝置上執行，而是在自家虛擬電腦上運作，即使使用者離線也能24小時持續執行。代價是代幣消耗速度也快，各訂閱方案每週配發固定代幣額度，用完後須加購額外點數。

產品 | 提供企業 | 主要特色 | 使用條件 
---|---|---|---
Grok Bot | SpaceXSI（xAI） | 多個具角色的Bot協同運作，支援定期執行 | 包含於X Premium以上方案（月費30至200美元，未稅） 
Dots | OpenAI | 以ChatGPT脈絡為起點執行調查與製作 | 分階段推出，Business Premium設有適用條件 
Muse | Meta | 確認郵件與行程並代為作業，基本功能免費 | 日本以iOS、Android、Web提供 

註：費率依各公司公開資料以月繳方式呈現。Grok Bot能否從日本簽約及各地區費率，須於簽約頁面確認。

馬斯克在10月29日的發文中，以超智慧將帶來富裕為前提，否定儲蓄的意義。然而AI代理的運作，實際上仍要負擔伺服器費用與電力。他本人終究還是碰上了營收與成本平衡這道經典經營課題。

競爭對手方面，Anthropic因Claude付費方案宣傳的使用額度與實際上限不符，遭到集體訴訟。緊縮使用額度的決定，也可視為規避同類訴訟風險的預防措施。記者向SpaceXSI查證，未能立即取得回覆。

另一方面，馬斯克在11月6日（當地時間）舉行的巴倫投資會議遠端對談中，對SpaceX成長展望端出強勁數字。他表示12月將達成年化營收逾1,000億美元（約3.3兆新台幣），明年12月則以年化經常性收入逾5,000億美元（約16.4兆新台幣）為目標。SpaceX去年營收僅約150億至160億美元（約5,200億新台幣），換算下來不到兩年要擴大約30倍以上。

他也提及由xAI主導的「Terafab」構想，目標是年產相當於1太瓦的AI晶片，規模約為明年全球AI晶片產量（預估約35至45吉瓦）的30倍。計畫在德州奧斯汀興建研發用晶圓廠，將設計、製造到測試集中在同一據點完成，以縮短開發週期。他認為：「原本要花1年的事，有可能縮短到1個月。」

至於資料中心業務，他說明若自行興建，工期8至9個月、投資額350億美元（約1.1兆新台幣）即可，遠低於委外所需的2年半、600億美元（約2兆新台幣）。在轉為自家Grok使用之前，將以每年約500億美元（約1.6兆新台幣）對外出租算力，藉此回收投資。

不過，當前市場環境並非全然順風。市場憂心11月期中選舉若民主黨奪回參眾兩院，資料中心監管將趨嚴，AI相關類股因而湧現賣壓，11月5日SpaceX股價重挫近9%，跌破6月首次公開募股（IPO）的發行價。特斯拉也下跌超過11%。加上主張暫停資料中心建設的候選人當選德州州長，更增添事業環境的不確定性。

姑且不論馬斯克「不必存錢」論是否站得住腳，AI代理越普及，推論成本就越膨脹。如何最佳化使用額度設計與收費體系，對旗下擁有Dots與Muse的競爭同業而言，同樣是共同課題。

xAI.title: 默认即标记：xAI 抢在欧盟大限前给 Grok 装上
xAI.description: 【导语】据 xAI 开发者文档与多家开发者媒体（DeAI、FreeAnswers 等）11 月 7 日报道，xAI 自 11 月 7 日起对 Grok API 的 7 个文本模型（grok-4.7、4.6、4.5、4.3 及 grok-4.20 的三个变体）默认开启不可见统计水印，覆盖普通文本、结构化输出与工具调用参数，开发者无需改动任何代码；每笔响应通过 x-watermark 响应头标出是否被标记。
xAI.content:
# 默认即标记：xAI 抢在欧盟大限前给 Grok 装上"隐形出生证"，却被自己一句话埋了雷

【导语】据 xAI 开发者文档与多家开发者媒体（DeAI、FreeAnswers 等）11 月 7 日报道，xAI 自 11 月 7 日起对 Grok API 的 7 个文本模型（grok-4.7、4.6、4.5、4.3 及 grok-4.20 的三个变体）默认开启不可见统计水印，覆盖普通文本、结构化输出与工具调用参数，开发者无需改动任何代码；每笔响应通过 x-watermark 响应头标出是否被标记。xAI 在文档中把理由直接写成"为遵守欧盟《AI 法案》"。

【为何重要】这不是一次普通的 API 小更新，而是主流前沿模型厂商第一次把"机器可读的内容标记"从可选动作变成默认动作。欧盟《AI 法案》第 50(2) 条要求生成式系统以机器可读方式标记合成内容，对 8 月 2 日前已在市系统设了宽限期，到 12 月 2 日截止——xAI 提前约三周"抢跑"，等于给同业立了一个事实标准：默认开、按模型开关、由团队管理员控制、需声明法律例外才能关。在 OpenAI 10 月初才开放"可选标记"、Anthropic 11 月初刚把水印扩到更多 Claude 模型的节奏下，xAI 这一步把竞争维度从"要不要标"推到了"怎么标、谁来关"。

【影响分析】对下游开发者，影响是静默而实在的：任何经 Grok API 产出的客服话术、公开文案或评测基线，自此都带着可被溯源的统计指纹，评测流水线跨 11 月 7 日前后会出现"两套生成机制"，缓存比对与确定性复现都要重做。对竞争格局，xAI 把合规成本前置成产品默认，反而可能削弱其"低监管姿态"的卖点——此前 xAI 消费端数据训练默认屡次反复，如今却最先向监管低头。受益方清晰：做内容溯源、AI 检测与合规中台的工具商拿到新增需求，而依赖"无缝转发 AI 文本"的仿冒链路被悄悄收紧。需要警惕的是，xAI 既声称水印"不影响质量与速度"，同一文档又承认它会"轻微影响模型挑选哪些 token"，这句自相矛盾的表述意味着质量影响尚未被独立评测证实，不能当作既成事实。

【未来趋势】未来 3 到 12 个月，三条信号值得盯：其一，OpenAI、Anthropic、Google 是否在 12 月 2 日前跟进默认水印，以及是否复制 xAI 的"团队管理员开关"结构；其二，独立研究者是否会发布同一 Grok 模型"带水印 vs 不带"的对照评测，给水印是否伤质量的争议定调；其三，被"锁定开启"的模型名单是否扩大——一旦锁死，xAI 文档里唯一的关闭入口也随之消失。预判/推测：若 12 月 2 日前另两家及以上前沿厂商未宣布等效默认水印、或仅以"可选"应付，则可证伪"欧盟第 50 条会立刻引发全行业默认标记"的判断，说明监管威慑仍停留在头部个案而非系统性合规。

【原创点评】我们认为，xAI 这一步与其说是"拥抱监管"，不如说是一次精算过的合规占位：用最低成本的默认开关，把"谁先被盯上"的风险转移给同行，同时把 EU AI Act 变成了自己的产品叙事。但真正的不确定性不在政策而在技术——当水印从"贴标签"变成"参与生成时选词"，它与模型安全边界（已有研究显示水印可能改变拒答行为）的耦合，远比一张合规清单更难算清。我们更倾向于把这次事件读作一个分水岭：生成式 AI 的"出生证"正从可选项变成出厂设置，而行业还没有为"带证模型"的质量与可控性准备好独立的度量衡。

# Underdog releases a 32MB voice model that runs entirely in the browser

Startup Underdog released a browser game using Woof, a 32MB speech model with 31 million parameters that runs entirely on-device without internet.

Startup Underdog has released an interactive browser game built on a speech generation model called Woof that is only 32MB in size. The model, which has 31 million parameters, runs entirely on-device without an internet connection - a direct challenge to the cloud-dependent approach of larger AI companies.

### A retro room that talks back

The demo, accessible through a web browser, places users in a room with a retro tech theme: a CRT monitor, a desk lamp with a clickable switch, and a typewriter. An introductory warning takes a jab at "intrusive" cloud providers. Users can type anything on the typewriter using their keyboard, and the game speaks it back through the Woof model. A music tuner in the room can also be rotated to generate different kinds of music.

The model is open for anyone to download. Underdog says it can run on most devices without internet connectivity. While a 32MB model won't replace large-scale speech systems, it points toward locally hosted assistants and personalized audio experiences that keep data on the user's hardware.

### Building a private AI stack

The Woof demo arrives weeks after Underdog launched Bark, a 167MB speech-to-text model also designed for edge devices. Founder Sigil Wen told TechCrunch he started the project because he wanted his own AI system rather than relying on cloud-based notetakers. "I think we will be able to run most capable models of today on the devices you already own within months," Wen said. "We just want to train the best open models that are American-made, that are open, that are capable and allow people to have private AI."

Underdog has also released a 27-billion-parameter model that can run on laptops, along with a waitlisted app positioned as a locally hosted alternative to tools like Muse and Instinct. The company's manifesto centers on open models and user-owned data - a stance that diverges from the centralized infrastructure powering most commercial AI services. For professionals exploring on-device AI, Generative AI Courses cover the fundamentals of how models like these are trained and deployed.

### Why this matters for creatives and writers

Small, offline-capable models change where and how creative work can happen. A writer drafting in a coffee shop with spotty Wi-Fi, a marketer prototyping voiceover for a campaign on a laptop, or an educator building interactive exercises without student data leaving the device - these scenarios become practical when models shrink to tens of megabytes. The ability to generate speech and music locally, without subscription fees or latency from cloud calls, lowers the barrier for experimentation.

On-device models also sidestep the privacy and ownership questions that come with uploading creative work to third-party servers. For anyone producing original audio content - podcasters, video editors, game developers - local generation means drafts and final assets stay under their control. Underdog's approach suggests that capable speech tools no longer require enterprise-scale infrastructure, which could reshape workflows for independent creators and small teams.

cross_cutting.content:
Bengaluru-based artificial intelligence startup Sarvam AI has launched Prism, a decision-making model built on its Sarvam 105B architecture, designed to help enterprises automate tasks requiring fast responses and confidence-based predictions.

The company said Prism can deliver responses in 44 milliseconds while achieving an average score of 71.8 across three evaluation benchmarks. The model is intended for enterprise applications including customer support, document processing, cybersecurity and AI agent management.

Prism is a Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuned version of Sarvam 105B. Unlike conventional large language models that generate responses sequentially, the new system processes inputs in a single forward pass and assigns probability scores to available options.

This approach allows organisations to use the model for classification and decision-making tasks without generating lengthy conversational responses.

According to Sarvam AI, Prism was evaluated against 24 other decision models on a single NVIDIA B200 GPU. The company reported that it achieved the highest average score among models operating with response times below 100 milliseconds.

Across three benchmarks, Prism recorded a score of 67 on the Jev Decision Index, 65.9 on the Artificial Analysis benchmark and 82.5 on an internal Indian-language evaluation.

The company has also developed the model to provide calibrated confidence scores, allowing businesses to establish thresholds for automated decisions and identify cases requiring human review.

Sarvam reported an error rate of 2.2% on English-language questions and 4.4% on Indian-language questions when the model's confidence level was at least 90%.

The company also assessed Prism's performance in AI agent monitoring, where the model achieved 86.4% accuracy in identifying agent activities requiring human review and 75% accuracy in determining whether tasks had been completed successfully.

In cybersecurity evaluations involving 5,517 questions across nine tasks, Prism recorded 89% accuracy. The assessments covered phishing detection, attempted jailbreaks and cybersecurity attack classification.

Sarvam said the model can evaluate an entire AI agent activity trace in approximately half a second on a single GPU and process inputs containing up to 131,072 tokens per question.

The company has released Prism's model weights on Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 licence, allowing developers and enterprises to fine-tune the technology using their own datasets.

Prism is also accessible through Sarvam's application programming interface (API) and can run in FP8 precision on a single GPU with at least 120 GB of memory.

The launch expands Sarvam AI's portfolio beyond general-purpose language models into specialised systems designed for operational decision-making.

Its intended applications include routing customer queries, selecting AI models for particular tasks, analysing documents and reviewing automated agent activity.

While the reported benchmark results indicate the model's performance under testing conditions, its effectiveness across different enterprise environments will depend on specific workloads and deployment requirements.
